title: AI across the flower business.
name: FiftyFlowers
short: AI for customer service, product image editing and company knowledge—in one internal platform.
problem: An online flower retailer has very different workflows across customer support, marketing and storefront operations. The challenge is connecting useful AI to each team’s actual information and tools.
contribution: Built and evolved the internal AI platform, support applications, a Chrome extension, marketing tools and commerce integrations. The work spans full-stack application development, cloud services, product-data workflows and visibility into the company’s AI roadmap.
groups: Customer service

Four applications for customer questions, reviews, claims and payment disputes, with shared chat, case history and a Chrome extension. The serving layer moved from AWS Lambda to Firebase and Google Cloud.
Company Second Brain

An umbrella MVP connecting departmental knowledge and tools. Customer Service knowledge, voice and policies support production apps; Marketing demonstrates image-tool guidance and presets; Engineering is a beta used in my own AI-assisted coding.
Marketing workflows

Image Studio supports consistent product photos, reusable presets and transparent cutouts. Farm Exports supports catalog-image work. The FAQ & Content Engine helps identify unanswered questions and review content drafts.
Shopping & operations

The flower-selection assistant, Share Your Flair wedding submissions and urgent-order requests connect storefront interactions with operational workflows. Earlier implementations and later improvements are distinct parts of the work.
Proposal Manager
Implemented supplied wireframes as a tool for event planning, flower recipes, presentations and shopping lists. It was not launched; work paused when DIY Migration took priority.
DIY Kits Migration
Tools match farm spreadsheets with store products and transfer kit recipes and purchase links to a test store, with source tracking and checks. Data cleanup and the production handoff remain ongoing.
Project visibility
A dedicated FiftyFlowers dashboard in The Record, linked from Internal AI, gives access to the AI roadmap, project milestones, completed work and evidence.
next: Continue the migration cleanup and handoff, and develop the company knowledge workspace beyond its MVP. Individual tools have different levels of maturity; the whole platform is not one finished autonomous system.
evidence: Scope reflects the reviewed project records and the saved September 2026 professional profile. The diagram is a capability map, not a screenshot or proof of company-wide adoption.

decisions: Bring related tools into one platform.
Evolved support applications, a browser extension, marketing tools and company knowledge into a shared internal platform, while retaining the different workflows each team needs.
Customer-service knowledge supports the operational apps. Marketing and engineering knowledge form developing parts of the broader company second brain; they are not presented as equally mature.

title: A clearer view of lending decisions.
name: Till
short: Machine-learning loan scoring saving $2,000 a month, with a five-view lending dashboard.
problem: Loan scoring needs to fit into an existing application process, while the team needs visibility into scoring activity and loan performance.
contribution: Built a machine-learning scoring service integrated with the lender’s application system, plus a dashboard for reviewing scoring activity, approval thresholds, lead sources and loan performance.
groups: Scoring API · $24K annualized savings
Machine-learning scores returned inside the existing loan application workflow. The service saves $2,000 per month; $24,000 expresses that saving over twelve months.
Overview · see the activity
Review scoring activity and decision patterns in one place.
Thresholds · manage policy
Review and adjust approval thresholds, with a recorded history of changes.
Lead Sources · compare channels
Explore where applications come from and how each source performs.
Funded History · follow performance
Review funded-loan history with clear reporting periods and funding definitions.
Scenario analysis · explore tradeoffs
Explore modeled exclusions alongside observed outcomes. Scenarios support investigation; they do not prove the effect of a policy change.
next: Scoring activity updates independently from imported loan-history data. Next steps focus on repeatable data refreshes and more precise links between policy changes and affected loans.
evidence: The workflow represents the documented service and dashboard. No customer applications or private financial records are included.

decisions: Protect policy changes from conflicting edits.
The policy editor checks the latest saved state before applying a change, preserves unrelated edits and keeps a change history. An adjustment is a recorded action, not an invisible replacement.
The analysis distinguishes observed funded outcomes from modeled exclusions. A scenario helps explore a decision; it is not presented as proof that a policy change caused an outcome.
decisionNote: These are documented implementation choices. Private policy settings, borrower information and model details are intentionally omitted.

title: Better systems for building systems.
name: AI Development Platform
short: A development suite for AI agents: project management, engineering memory and orchestration.
problem: AI-assisted work can lose context across sessions and scatter decisions across repositories, conversations and tools. Planning and delivery need a shared structure that humans can inspect.
contribution: Built an internal product suite around three distinct responsibilities: managing the work, retaining engineering knowledge and supervising agent assignments. These tools support my own development process; deeper integration remains in development.
groups: The Record · manage the work
A project-management system for developers, clients and connected coding agents. It organizes scoped milestones, progress, decisions and evidence of completed work in a shared workspace.
Brain · preserve the context
Reusable engineering memory for project context, repository knowledge, decisions, workflows and handoffs across coding sessions.
Jarvis OS · coordinate execution
Orchestration for assigning and supervising coding agents, connecting their work with project context and engineering knowledge.
The working cycle

Plan a bounded milestone, pursue that work, capture questions and evidence, then review the outcome before planning the next scope. Engineering judgment and release accountability stay with the developer.
next: Bring project context and engineering memory into a more unified assistant experience. The complete proposed integration is not presented as a finished autonomous platform.
evidence: This is a conceptual map of the actual product responsibilities. It deliberately omits private prompts, credentials and implementation details.

decisions: Give each product a clear responsibility.

The Record holds project scope and evidence, Brain retains engineering context, and Jarvis OS explores supervised agent execution. Keeping those responsibilities explicit makes unfinished integration visible.
Treat work as a reviewable scope.
Milestones group related features, their environment and evidence. Planning defines the next scope; execution updates the record; review decides what happens next.
decisionNote: The Record and Brain support the development workflow. Deeper integration with Jarvis OS is the next step.

title: From business reports to useful answers.
name: Create Spaces
short: Booking reports become a workspace for sales trends, export visibility and AI answers with cited sources.
problem: Sales information was locked inside reports. The team needed a way to collect them, understand bookings and ask follow-up questions without losing the original source.
contribution: Built the cloud report-export workflow and a local reporting workspace. It connects booking data, saved PDFs, export visibility and AI questions with cited report pages.
groups: Understand bookings
Review booking data with coverage and freshness visible alongside the figures.
Ask questions · inspect the answer
Reports & AI opens cited PDF pages and highlights source text beside the conversation.
Keep the history
Saved report versions retain their dates and original PDFs, so an answer can be checked against its source.
See what is collected
Export and spending views show managed reports, collection activity and cost.
next: The workspace runs locally and connects to private cloud storage. Sustained daily reliability, company hosting, shared conversation history and conversational dashboard editing remain in development.
evidence: The September 24 screenshots show the earlier local reporting interface, with confidential values redacted. AI questions and source highlighting were verified in the current code and project record; they are not pictured in this set. The screenshots do not prove uninterrupted daily reliability.

decisions: Verify a report before replacing the current data.

The export workflow independently checks the report before accepting a new version. A failed check keeps the last accepted dataset available instead of promoting incomplete or inconsistent information.
Retain the source, not just the dashboard.
Saved report versions and their original PDFs remain part of the reporting workspace. That makes the displayed information traceable to an accepted export.
decisionNote: Working local software connected to private cloud storage. Company deployment and sustained daily reliability remain ahead; the screenshots predate the cited AI workspace.
